guidance.name: Easy or Aerobic Run Day
guidance.purpose: Support normal aerobic training while maintaining recovery and appetite control.
guidance.hydration: Normal daily hydration plus fluids lost during training.
guidance.coachFocus: Keep protein consistent and place some carbohydrate before and after the run.

guidance.name: Recovery or Rest Day
guidance.purpose: Maintain muscle repair and general recovery when training demand is low.
guidance.hydration: Maintain normal hydration; replace any remaining losses from the previous day.
simpleExamples: lean meat with vegetables and rice
guidance.coachFocus: Keep protein high, reduce carbohydrate only modestly, and prioritise fruit and vegetables.

guidance.name: Interval or VO2 Session Day
guidance.purpose: Fuel a demanding quality session and replenish carbohydrate afterwards.
guidance.hydration: Begin well hydrated and replace sweat losses after training.
simpleExamples: burrito with extra rice and lean protein
guidance.coachFocus: Include an easy-to-digest carbohydrate meal or snack before training and a carbohydrate-plus-protein meal afterwards.

guidance.name: Tempo or Threshold Day
guidance.purpose: Support sustained quality running without excessive gastrointestinal load.
guidance.hydration: Normal daily hydration plus replacement of session losses.
simpleExamples: banana before training and yoghurt afterwards.
guidance.coachFocus: Spread carbohydrate across the day and avoid a very high-fat meal immediately before the session.

guidance.name: Long Run Day
guidance.purpose: Provide sufficient carbohydrate before, during and after a long endurance session.
guidance.hydration: Start hydrated, drink according to conditions and duration, and replace fluid and sodium afterwards.
guidance.duringTraining: For longer runs, practise the same carbohydrate and hydration strategy intended for race day.
simpleExamples: Toast, oats and banana before running
sports drink or gels during longer sessions
chicken and rice, pasta with lean meat, salmon and potatoes, fruit and yoghurt afterwards.
guidance.coachFocus: Prioritise carbohydrate availability and practise race-compatible foods rather than experimenting on key days.

guidance.name: Day Before a Long Run
guidance.purpose: Top up glycogen and hydration without requiring an extreme carb load.
guidance.hydration: Drink regularly through the day and include normal dietary sodium.
simpleExamples: yoghurt, bananas and cereal as snacks.
guidance.coachFocus: Increase carbohydrate portions, keep meals familiar, and avoid turning dinner into an unusually large or greasy meal.

guidance.name: Upper-Body Strength Day
guidance.purpose: Support strength performance and muscle repair with moderate carbohydrate demand.
guidance.hydration: Normal daily hydration plus training losses.
guidance.coachFocus: Distribute protein across three to five meals and include carbohydrate around training.

guidance.name: Lower-Body Strength Day
guidance.purpose: Support a more demanding strength session and recovery of the legs.
guidance.hydration: Normal daily hydration plus training losses.
guidance.coachFocus: Treat a hard lower-body session more like a quality running day than a rest day.

guidance.name: Soccer or Futsal Day
guidance.purpose: Fuel repeated high-intensity efforts and replace carbohydrate and fluid afterwards.
guidance.hydration: Begin hydrated and replace sweat and sodium after play, especially in warm indoor venues.
simpleExamples: pasta or rice with protein afterwards.
guidance.coachFocus: Avoid treating soccer as a low-load social session; fuel it like a quality workout.

guidance.name: Double-Session Day
guidance.purpose: Support two training sessions while maintaining recovery between them.
guidance.hydration: Replace fluid and sodium after the first session before beginning the second.
simpleExamples: rice with chicken after session one
pasta, potatoes or rice with lean protein at dinner.
guidance.coachFocus: Eat between sessions rather than trying to make up the entire day at dinner.

guidance.name: Race Week
guidance.purpose: Maintain normal nutrition early in the week and gradually increase carbohydrate as race day approaches.

macros.carbohydrates: 4–7 g/kg/day, increasing toward the upper end near the event.
macros.fat: Moderate early in the week and slightly lower as carbohydrate portions rise.

guidance.hydration: Maintain steady hydration rather than trying to correct everything the night before.
simpleExamples: Familiar rice, pasta, bread, oats, fruit, potatoes, lean meat, fish and yoghurt-based meals.
guidance.coachFocus: Keep foods familiar, reduce unnecessary experimentation, and avoid overeating simply because training volume has dropped.

guidance.name: Marathon Carb-Loading Day
guidance.purpose: Maximise carbohydrate availability before a marathon or similarly long race.

macros.carbohydrates: 7–10 g/kg/day when a deliberate carb load is appropriate.
macros.fat: Lower than normal to make room for carbohydrate without excessive total food volume.

guidance.hydration: Drink normally and include sodium with meals; avoid forcing excessive plain water.
simpleExamples: White rice, pasta, bread, cereal, oats, bananas, juice, low-fat yoghurt, lean chicken, simple sandwiches and familiar carbohydrate snacks.
guidance.coachFocus: Use lower-fibre, familiar carbohydrate foods and spread intake across the day.

guidance.name: Race Morning
guidance.purpose: Provide familiar, digestible carbohydrate before racing.

macros.protein: Small to moderate amount if normally tolerated.
macros.carbohydrates: A carbohydrate-focused meal several hours before the start, scaled to body size and tolerance.

guidance.hydration: Arrive hydrated without excessive last-minute drinking.
simpleExamples: a familiar small coffee when normally used.
guidance.coachFocus: Nothing new on race morning. Use the exact foods and timing already tested in long runs.

guidance.name: Post-Race or Very Long Session
guidance.purpose: Begin carbohydrate replenishment, muscle repair and rehydration after a major endurance effort.

macros.carbohydrates: 5–8 g/kg/day depending on the event and how soon normal training resumes.
macros.fat: Normal moderate intake once appetite and digestion settle.

guidance.hydration: Replace fluid and sodium progressively rather than all at once.
guidance.coachFocus: Start with easy-to-eat food, then return to normal balanced meals rather than relying only on snacks.

guidance.name: Hot-Weather Training Day
guidance.purpose: Support training when fluid and electrolyte losses are likely to be elevated.

macros.protein: Use the range appropriate to the training session.
macros.carbohydrates: Use the range appropriate to the training session.
macros.fat: Use the range appropriate to the training session.

guidance.hydration: Begin hydrated, drink to a practical plan during longer sessions, and replace fluid and sodium afterwards.
simpleExamples: fruit, yoghurt, rice bowls, sandwiches and salty recovery meals.
guidance.coachFocus: Adjust fluid and sodium more than macros unless heat materially changes session duration or intensity.
